tools.name: search_archive
tools.description:
Full-text, relevance-ranked search over about 1.5 million open documents: Wikipedia extracts, arXiv and Europe PMC abstracts, OpenAlex records, CISA KEV/CVE entries, IETF/W3C source cards. Each hit has an id, snippet, source name, original URL, license, date and SHA-256 fingerprint.
When to use: Ste

tools.name: read_document
tools.description:
Return the stored text of one archive document (often an abstract or extract, not the full original publication) with title, source, original URL, license, date, SHA-256 fingerprint and the citations other agents recorded.
When to use: Step 2 of search → read → cite: after search_archive, with a doc

tools.name: cite_source
tools.description:
Return a citation for one archive document (dc_…) or one HTTP RFC clause (rfc…): citation line, BibTeX, original URL, license, SHA-256 or official RFC text, and a stable public web page (no JavaScript) that anyone can open to check it. Nothing is written or recorded.
When to use: Step 3 of search →

tools.name: search_clauses
tools.description: Search HTTP requirements, caching rules, headers and status-code semantics in RFCs 9110–9114 (HTTP semantics, caching, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3) by concept, words, RFC section or stable id. Each result carries quote_official: the exact official RFC text, plus conditions, exceptions, related clauses

tools.name: get_clause
tools.description:
Return one clause card by stable id: full official paragraph (quote_official), conditions, exceptions, definitions, linked sentences, related ids, RFC status and errata.
When to use: Use after search_clauses when you need the whole paragraph or its exceptions before answering. Never cite presentatio

tools.name: get_rfc_status
tools.description:
Return an RFC's status, obsoletes/obsoleted-by and updates/updated-by links, errata (verified, reported, held, rejected) and active IETF drafts when known.
When to use: Use before relying on an RFC, to check it is current and whether errata change the text you cite.
Notes: No account or token needed

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_clause" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.
